title: Ashtpadi 19, salok: nothing goes along
hook: nothing goes with you except devotion (Sukhmani 19)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Panj Pyare, and your line: both ways. Did you keep the one practice you chose? Today Sukhmani enters its last stretch, ashtpadis nineteen to twenty-four, and the nineteenth begins with a hard look at what we own. Day five hundred ten.

Anyone who has cleared out a parent's home knows the feeling. The drawers of rubber bands. The good china used twice. The boxes of papers that once mattered terribly: tax forms, warranties, letters. A lifetime of things, and all of it, every last bit, stayed behind. You stand in the half-empty room holding a coffee mug and realize the person isn't in any of it. The salok of the nineteenth ashtpadi says this out loud, and then says what isn't left behind. Today: nothing goes along.
screen: `CLEARING OUT A PARENT'S HOME.` → `A LIFETIME OF THINGS, ALL LEFT.` → `THE PERSON ISN'T IN ANY OF IT.`

segments.voice: The salok, in paraphrase: nothing goes along with you except devotion; all the poison of worldly things is ash. Earn the Name of the Lord; Nanak, this is the excellent wealth. Three words open it. Saath: with, alongside, company. Na chaalai: does not go. Bin bhajan: except devotion, the singing and remembering of God. So the first line is a short inventory. Everything you own, check the list, and next to almost every item: does not go. Then the strong image: bikhiaa saglee chhaar. Bikhiaa is a word Gurbani uses for maya's poison, the pull of worldly things. Chhaar is ash. Not evil, exactly. Ash: what's left when the fire has burned out. The house, the car, the savings account aren't wicked. They're just ash-in-waiting. Then the turn, and it's a money word. Kamaavanaa: to earn. Earn the Name. The salok doesn't tell you to stop earning; Sikhs are expected to work honestly and provide for their families. It tells you what else to earn. And it calls the Name dhan, wealth, and saar, the excellent, the essential. So this isn't a hymn against wealth. It's a hymn about which wealth travels. Over the next days the ashtpadi will look at what stays behind and what does go along. Today, only the inventory. And notice that the salok makes no threat. It simply points at the room full of things and says: none of this comes with you, except the devotion.
screen: `SAATH NA CHAALAI: DOES NOT GO ALONG.` · `BIKHIAA IS ASH: CHHAAR.` · `KAMAAVANAA: EARN THE NAME.` · `WHICH WEALTH TRAVELS?` · then, large: `NOTHING GOES ALONG.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: look at your possessions. Let your eyes move slowly around the room you're in: the furniture, the phone, the clothes, the books, the screen. To each thing, without judging it, say silently: this stays. Not with sadness; just accurately. Then, at the end, close your eyes and ask: what, if anything, is going along with me? Let the question sit without answering it. The bell holds the time.
Saath, with or alongside: its salok says saath na chaalai bin bhajan, nothing goes along except devotion; earn the Name, the excellent wealth.
Your line: nothing goes along. Today, before you buy something, pause and say silently: this stays. Then decide. Day five hundred ten.

howItsDone: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib open the nineteenth ashtpadi with the salok saath na chaalai bin bhajan, and Sikh life pairs honest earning with remembering the Name as the wealth that lasts.

match.prompt: the salok of ashtpadi 19 — tap the pairs.

myth: the salok tells Sikhs to stop earning money
it says what else to earn: the Name, the excellent wealth.
the salok calls the Name a kind of wealth
dhan saar: the excellent, essential wealth.
the salok calls worldly things wicked
it calls them ash: what remains when the fire has burned out.

fork.setup: you're clearing out a loved one's home after they've died. what does the nineteenth salok say went along with them?
fork.reveal: saath na chaalai bin bhajan: nothing goes along except devotion. the things are ash; the Name is the wealth that travels.

original.note: Gurmukhi: saath, with, alongside, as in saath na chaalai, does not go along.

trapdoor: what you thought: you can't take it with you, so don't bother.
what it means: work and earn, but earn the Name too, the one wealth that travels.
what a scholar hears: the salok uses market language, kamaavanaa (earn) and dhan (wealth), for devotion, and bikhiaa for maya's poison, a frequent Gurbani term.

sources.ref: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 19, salok (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 288)

notes: Salok of ashtpadi 19 paraphrased: saath na chaalai bin bhajan bikhiaa saglee chhaar; har har naam kamaavanaa Nanak ih dhan saar. Confirm Ang 288.
Gloss of bikhiaa as maya's poison: confirm.
Audit (2026-10-01): the teach said the salok makes 'no promise about what happens after we die', which contradicts its own line that devotion goes along; that clause is removed.
